lines.japanese: 往くか、留まるか。
lines.english: To go, or to remain.

lines.japanese: 「帰ろ？」
lines.english: “Want to go home?”

lines.japanese: 僕は優しい声に後ろ髪を引かれていた。
lines.english: The gentle voice made me reluctant to leave.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君？　なに？　どうしたの？」
lines.english: “Haneda? What is it? What’s wrong?”

lines.japanese: そのせいか、グレタガルドへの旅路がいつもより長く感じられたんだ。
lines.english: Perhaps that was why the journey to Gretagard felt longer than usual.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君？　大丈夫？　顔真っ白だよ！？」
lines.english: “Haneda? Are you all right? Your face is completely white!”

lines.japanese: 僕を案じる女のひとの声は、飛びたとうとした僕に幾ばくかの未練を残す。
lines.english: The concern in her voice left me with one last attachment to this world as I prepared to fly.

lines.japanese: 往くか、留まるか。
lines.english: To go, or to remain.

lines.japanese: 楽園の蜃気楼と、彼女のいる凍えた大地の狭間で、僕はぐずぐずと逡巡した。
lines.english: Suspended between a mirage of paradise and the frozen earth where she waited, I lingered in indecision.

lines.japanese: そして誰かの──たぶん僕のだ──夢見るような声が、答えを出した。
lines.english: Then someone’s voice—mine, perhaps—gave the answer in a dreamlike murmur.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、こっちの世界は息苦しい……ちょっと……ちょっとだけ、行ってくるね……」
lines.english: “Ah, it is so hard to breathe in this world... I'm just... I'm just going over there for a little while...”

lines.japanese: 「行くって、どこに」
lines.english: “Going where?”

lines.japanese: 「グレタガルドだよ……早く行かなくちゃ……」
lines.english: “To Gretagard… I have to hurry…”

lines.japanese: 僕らの声はどこか遠くて、それはまるで、起き抜けの夢うつつに流れている感度の悪いラジオみたいだ。
lines.english: Our voices sounded far away, like a poorly tuned radio playing through the waking haze of a dream.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君。羽田君、聞こえる？」
lines.english: “Haneda. Haneda, can you hear me?”

lines.japanese: とうとう決断した僕に、しかし彼女が追いすがる。
lines.english: Even after I had finally made my choice, she pursued me.

lines.japanese: 彼女は──渡来さんは──僕に残っていてほしいのだろうか。
lines.english: Did she—did Watarai—want me to stay?

lines.japanese: 僕に残っていてほしいなんて思ってくれるひとが、まだ向こうにもいたのだろうか。
lines.english: Was there still someone on that side who wanted me to stay?

lines.japanese: だったら……まだ……もう少しぐらい……。
lines.english: If so… perhaps… just a little longer…

lines.japanese: 揺らぐ決意。往くか、留まるか。
lines.english: My resolve wavered. To go, or to remain.

lines.japanese: けれど黄金色の塵埃に汚染されたあそこの空は、不器用な僕が気ままに生きてゆくにはあまりに厳しい。
lines.english: And yet the sky in that world, polluted with golden dust, was far too harsh for a clumsy creature like me to live beneath it as I pleased.

lines.japanese: 「だって……僕たちには……」
lines.english: “Because we…”

lines.japanese: 「僕たちには翼がないんだ……」
lines.english: “We have no wings…”

lines.japanese: なのに、大好きな優しい声が迷わせる。
lines.english: And still the gentle voice I loved made me hesitate.

lines.japanese: もしも君が望むなら僕は。
lines.english: If you wished it, I would—

lines.japanese: 往くか、留まるか。
lines.english: To go, or to remain.

lines.japanese: 往くか、往かざるか。
lines.english: To go, or not to go.

lines.japanese: 逝くべきか、生きつづけるべきか。
lines.english: To die, or to go on living.

lines.japanese: そしてとうとう、決めあぐねた僕の≪精髄≫は──
lines.english: At last, unable to decide, my essence—

lines.japanese: ──美空学園でもグレタガルドでもない、中二階とでも呼ぶべき半端なところに引っかかった。
lines.english: —caught in an unfinished place between them, neither Misora Academy nor Gretagard: a mezzanine, perhaps.

lines.japanese: 往くか、留まるか。決断までの猶予期間が与えられたのかもしれない。
lines.english: To go, or to remain. Perhaps I had been granted a little time before the decision came due.

lines.japanese: 優柔不断な僕はどこでもどこまでもモラトリアムなんだ。
lines.english: Indecisive as ever, wherever I went, I could only put life off a little longer.

lines.japanese: “やれやれタカシ君はまた逃げちゃったのか”
lines.english: “Good grief. Takashi has run away again, has he?”

lines.japanese: 墜ちてきた僕と入れかわりに、誰かが横を通りすぎて昇っていった。
lines.english: As I fell, someone passed beside me and ascended in my place.

lines.japanese: 彼は誰で、僕の何で、どこへ向かったのか。そんなことは知らない……はずなのに、なぜか知っているような気もした。
lines.english: Who was he? What was he to me? Where was he going? I should not have known any of it… and yet somehow I felt that I did.

lines.japanese: 懐かしさのような既視感。
lines.english: Déjà vu tinged with nostalgia.

lines.japanese: 赤ん坊のころ生きわかれて顔を知らないはずの子供でも、親は再会した瞬間に自分との結びつきを直感するっていう。
lines.english: They say that even if a parent and child are parted when the child is an infant—before the parent can know the face the child will grow into—the parent recognizes their bond the instant they meet again.

lines.japanese: それと同じようなことなのだと思う。僕は一切の当惑もなく、ごく自然に確信していた。
lines.english: I thought this must be something like that. I was certain of it, naturally and without the slightest confusion.

lines.japanese: 何故だか“思いだす”というプロセスすら経ずに、何故だか僕はその瞬間それを“知って”いた。
lines.english: Somehow I never even passed through the process of “remembering.” Somehow, in that instant, I simply “knew.”

lines.japanese: 彼は僕らのうちの一人だ。
lines.english: He was one of us.

lines.japanese: 僕ら？　ああそうか、僕は僕だけじゃなかったんだ。
lines.english: Us? Ah, of course. I was never only me.

lines.japanese: 僕は普通じゃなかったんだ。
lines.english: I was not ordinary.

lines.japanese: ああ、なあんだ。
lines.english: Ah. So that was all.

lines.japanese: 「この子、本物だ！」
lines.english: “This boy is the real thing!”

lines.japanese: 彼女の声にも興奮が窺えた。
lines.english: Excitement showed even in her voice.

lines.japanese: ふうん。
lines.english: I see.

lines.japanese: それじゃあ彼女が──渡来さんがときおり向ける僕への興味深い視線は、青春の甘い情動とは無関係の、単なる好奇心だったのかな。
lines.english: Had those searching looks she—Watarai—sometimes gave me been nothing more than curiosity, with none of the tender passions of youth?

lines.japanese: なあんだ……やっぱり行こうかな、グレタガルド。
lines.english: So that was it… Perhaps I should go to Gretagard after all.

lines.japanese: しょせん僕が敬愛されるヒーローになりうるのは、向こうの世界だけじゃないか。
lines.english: After all, the only world where I could ever become a beloved hero was the one on the other side.

lines.japanese: 「はねだくん……？」
lines.english: “Haneda…?”

lines.japanese: 珍種のペットでも撫でるような甘い声で、渡来さんが僕の抜け殻に語りかけている。
lines.english: In a sweet voice fit for soothing some rare and curious creature, Watarai spoke to the empty shell I had left behind.

lines.japanese: なんだか無性に笑いたくなった。
lines.english: I was seized by an irresistible urge to laugh.

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth*.

lines.japanese: 「えーと、はい」
lines.english: “Um… yes.”

lines.japanese: だけど僕は笑っていなかった。僕じゃない僕が、僕の名を呼ばれて僕のように答えていた。
lines.english: But I had not laughed. A me who was not me had heard my name and answered in my voice.

lines.japanese: 「なにかな？」
lines.english: “What is it?”

lines.japanese: 彼はなんとか僕のふりをして窮地を脱しようとしている。彼はいつもこうして、僕が飛んだあとの後始末をしてくれていたから──ああ、そんなことまで“知って”いるんだ。
lines.english: He was doing his best to impersonate me and escape this predicament. This was what he always did: he cleaned up the mess after I flew away—and, ah, I knew that too.

lines.japanese: いまの僕は随分といろいろなことを“知って”いる。
lines.english: At present, I knew a remarkable number of things.

lines.japanese: だけど、ここでは当たり前のように“知って”いる事実も、元の世界へ戻ったときにはすべて忘れているんだろう。
lines.english: But every fact I knew here as a matter of course would surely be forgotten when I returned to the original world.

lines.japanese: でも、それはちょうど都合が良いのかもしれない。
lines.english: Maybe that was for the best.

lines.japanese: だって、ここでの僕は“知って”いるのが自然だから受けいれるまでもなく受けいれているけど、美空学園の僕はきっとこの事実を受けいれることが出来ないだろう。
lines.english: Here, knowing was so natural that I accepted these things without even having to accept them. But the me at Misora Academy would surely be incapable of accepting the truth.

lines.japanese: いや違う、逆だ。
lines.english: No. That was wrong. It was the reverse.

lines.japanese: 受けいれることが出来ないから、忘れてしまうんだ。
lines.english: I forgot because I could not accept it.

lines.japanese: “知って”いたくないから“知って”いないことになるんだ。
lines.english: Because I did not want to know, it became something I did not know.

lines.japanese: だから僕はグレタガルドでのことや──
lines.english: That was why I forgot everything about Gretagard, and—

lines.japanese: ──あっ！
lines.english: —ah!

lines.japanese: そう。そのとき僕はもう自然と“知って”いた。
lines.english: Yes. By then I already knew, as naturally as breathing.

lines.japanese: なあんだ、グレタガルドって僕の妄想だったんだあ！
lines.english: Oh, of course! Gretagard was only a fantasy I had invented!

lines.japanese: けれど現実世界の僕は、きっとその事実を拒絶するだろう。
lines.english: But the me in the real world would surely reject that truth.

lines.japanese: だから僕は厳しい現実へ帰るのも、妄想上の楽園へ飛ぶのも嫌になって、とりあえずこの半端な≪中二階≫で眠ることにした。
lines.english: And so I lost the desire both to return to harsh reality and to fly away to an imaginary paradise. For the moment, I decided to sleep here in this unfinished mezzanine between the two.

lines.japanese: 子供のころの夢。目を覚ましたとき、小人さんが宿題をぜんぶ片付けてくれてたらいいな。
lines.english: A childhood dream. When I woke up, perhaps the little elves would have finished all my homework for me.

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth*.

lines.japanese: たしか≪中二階≫で僕が見たのはこんな夢だった。
lines.english: As I recalled, this was the dream I saw in the mezzanine.

lines.japanese: あかね色に染まった取調室。僕じゃない僕は数々の詰問を漂々とかわして、その場から離脱しようとするのだけれど、優しい声の尋問官は実に豊富な手札を持っていた。
lines.english: An interrogation room stained sunset-red. The me who was not me airily parried question after question as he tried to extricate himself, but the interrogator with the gentle voice held a formidable hand of cards.

lines.japanese: 僕じゃない僕は、なかば白旗を揚げていた。
lines.english: The me who was not me already had his white flag halfway up.

lines.japanese: 「グレタガルド、聖騎士ホーク、異世界への旅……あーそうすかー、ずいぶん喋っちゃったんだ……」
lines.english: “Gretagard, the Holy Knight Hawk, journeys to another world… Oh, I see. He told you quite a lot, didn’t he…”

lines.japanese: 「あ。念のため聞くけど、実はぼく夢を見て寝ぼけてたんすよ、なんつったら信じてくれます？」
lines.english: “Oh. Just to be safe, let me ask: would you believe me if I said I’d been half-asleep and talking about a dream?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、厳しいですね。たとえそれは信じたとして……じゃあ私がきのう会った、まるで別人みたいにおっかない羽田君についてはどう説明してくれるんでしょう」
lines.english: “Hmm. That would be difficult. Even if I believed that… how would you explain the terrifying Haneda I met yesterday, who seemed like an entirely different person?”

lines.japanese: 「それに私、細々とした疑惑なら他にいくつも挙げられますよ。羽田君のことなら三年間ずっと見てきましたから」
lines.english: “Besides, I could name any number of smaller suspicions. I’ve been watching you for three full years, Haneda.”

lines.japanese: 「あらら。君はぼくの何なのさ」
lines.english: “Goodness. And what exactly are you to me?”

lines.japanese: 「公称、彼女」
lines.english: “Officially? Your girlfriend.”

lines.japanese: 「公称。それは何、好きなの、好きじゃないの？」
lines.english: “Officially. What does that mean? Do you like me, or don’t you?”

lines.japanese: 「いいひとだと思う」
lines.english: “I think you’re a good person.”

lines.japanese: 「いいひとだけど好きではない？」
lines.english: “A good person, but not somebody you like?”

lines.japanese: 「好きですよ。恋っていうのとは違うと思うけども、感謝してるし尊敬に値するし、人間として好きかな」
lines.english: “I do like you. I don’t think it’s the same as being in love, but I’m grateful to you, and you deserve my respect. I suppose I like you as a person.”

lines.japanese: 「わお、綺麗な逃げ方」
lines.english: “Wow. What an elegant escape.”

lines.japanese: 「実際、好きとか恋とか、そういう次元の感情じゃあないよね。共感……っていうのかな、羽田君には同じにおいを感じるっていうか」
lines.english: “Honestly, this isn't really a feeling on the level of liking someone or being in love. Empathy… maybe? There's something kindred about you, like we carry the same scent.”

lines.japanese: 「軽はずみなことは言いたくないですけど、私ならそこらの誰かよりは、羽田君のこと分かってあげられると思います」
lines.english: “I don’t want to speak carelessly, but I think I could understand you better than some random person ever could.”

lines.japanese: 「……悪いようにはしないと？」
lines.english: “…You're saying you won't do me wrong?”

lines.japanese: 「ヤな言い方すんな。助け合いたいんです」
lines.english: “Don’t make it sound so ugly. I want us to help each other.”

lines.japanese: 「助け“合う”？　なんすかそれ？」
lines.english: “Each other? What’s that supposed to mean?”

lines.japanese: 「まずは友達になろうと思ってます。詳しいことは、そちらが教えてくれたら、こちらも教えます」
lines.english: “For a start, I intend to become your friend. As for the details: if you tell me what you know, I’ll tell you what I know.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ……その取引は、なんかこっちに得があるんすかね」
lines.english: “Huh… And is there some benefit in that arrangement for me?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ？　まだ聞いてないのに、そんなの分かりません。ただ、力になれることなら協力は惜しまないつもりです」
lines.english: “How should I know? I haven’t heard anything yet. But if there’s some way I can help, I intend to give you my full cooperation.”

lines.japanese: 「ああそう。じゃあ最初のお願い、当面のところタカシ君には何も話さないどいてね。彼ショック受けちゃうから。ヘタしたらグレタガルドに引きこもっちゃうかも」
lines.english: “Oh, I see. Then here’s my first request: for the time being, don’t tell Takashi anything. He’d be shocked. If things went badly, he might shut himself away in Gretagard.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　なにそれ、どういう──」
lines.english: “What? What does that—”

lines.japanese: 「こっちの質問が先。タカシ君に話さないって誓える？」
lines.english: “My question first. Can you swear you won’t tell Takashi?”

lines.japanese: 「う……うん、誓う」
lines.english: “I… Yes. I swear.”

lines.japanese: 「天の神様に誓える？」
lines.english: “Can you swear it to God in heaven?”

lines.japanese: 「分かりました。今はもういない私の弟に誓いましょう」
lines.english: “Very well. I swear it on my little brother, who is no longer with us.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぅー……」
lines.english: “Phew…”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、まあ、いっかあ。ヨージ君は相変わらずだし、隼人君は先に行っちゃったし、俺もそろそろかなって感じだし──」
lines.english: “Well, then, I suppose it’s all right. Yoji is the same as ever, Hayato has gone on ahead, and I have the feeling my own time is coming soon—”

lines.japanese: 「──かと言って俺が行ったあと、彼の面倒を小鳩さん一人に任せるのも心配だもんなあ」
lines.english: “—but once I’m gone, I’d hate to leave Kobato alone with the burden of looking after him.”

lines.japanese: 「は、はあ？」
lines.english: “E-excuse me?”

lines.japanese: 「ああスイマセン、申しおくれました。俺は千歳鷲介。渉外担当の≪外交官≫、人呼んでぬるぬる鷲介。余命いくばくもない潤滑油ですコンバンワ」
lines.english: “Ah, forgive me. I neglected to introduce myself. I’m Shusuke Chitose, liaison officer and resident diplomat, better known as Slippery Shusuke—the lubricating oil that’s not long for this world. A very good evening to you.”

lines.japanese: 「さてさて、お姫様。まあ立ち話もなんでしょうから、歩きながら話しましょうかね」
lines.english: “Now then, Princess. Standing here talking won't do, so shall we continue as we walk?”
